source_verification.note: The dispatch named three claims to check hardest. Each was checked against source read in this session, not against the author's or researcher's report of it.
source_verification.release_and_artifacts: Correct as stated. The page links the floating index https://github.com/XXJones21/Hearth/releases and names v0.1.0-alpha, dated 2026-08-22, as what is published there today. wiki/releasing.md:208 records `0.1.0 alpha, published 2026-08-22, shipped Windows, macOS and Android`, and wiki/releasing.md:199-204 records that artifacts and a SHA256SUMS.txt go to the GitHub release. The artifact list on the page matches the table at wiki/releasing.md:37-42 exactly: `.exe` and `.msi` for Windows, `.dmg` for Apple Silicon macOS, `.apk` for Android, and no iOS or visionOS asset, which wiki/releasing.md:44-45 states is still outstanding. I have no network tool, so I could not refetch the release itself; the corpus corroboration is what I can establish by reading, and it agrees with the research artifact on every point.
source_verification.signing_and_the_macos_caveat: Honest and correctly placed. `Only the Android build is signed` matches wiki/releasing.md:47, and `neither signed nor notarized` matches the macOS row at wiki/releasing.md:40. The page's onward pointer is also right: the extra first-open step lives at wiki/installing.md:76-88 under `Open Hearth for the first time on macOS`, which is the page the sentence links, so the reader is not sent somewhere the step is missing.
source_verification.windows_three_bands: Stated correctly, and the correction the task exists to make is sound. The mechanism is confirmed at crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:128-158: the coexist arm at 128-136, the take-turns arm at 137-150 whose warning is `Your persona will think and speak one at a time`, and PlanError::TooSmall at 151-157 as the only refusal. I recomputed both boundaries from the constants rather than accepting them. Windows is not unified (machine.rs:82), so base is stt_bytes 805306368 plus headroom_bytes 1073741824 = 1879048192 (dictionary.yaml:84, 89). Windows is in cpp_platforms (dictionary.yaml:102), so the voice holds 966367641 (dictionary.yaml:113). The smallest thing that can fit is tier 0's Q3_K_M at 2536786016 (dictionary.yaml:176) plus the MIN_CTX floor of 12288 x 4096 = 50331648, which fit_at at plan.rs:300-313 requires, so 2587117664. Refusal therefore begins below 1879048192 + 2587117664 = 4466165856 bytes, and both model and voice stay resident from 1879048192 + 966367641 + 2587117664 = 5432533497 bytes upward. Those are 4.47 GB and 5.43 GB in decimal gigabytes, which is what the page's `roughly 4.5 GB` and `roughly 5.4 GB` state. The old 8 GB video-memory floor was wrong by nearly a factor of two and is gone.
source_verification.windows_unit_caveat: One qualification, recorded as a further improvement rather than a finding because no real card falls in the disputed window. crates/hearth-probe/src/lib.rs:24-35 prints GiB under a `GB` label, with the comment that GiB `is what a user comparing against their spec sheet expects`. In those units the same two boundaries read 4.16 GB and 5.06 GB, so the page's figures sit about eight percent above the numbers the product itself will show a refused reader. Checked against real card sizes: a 4 GB card (4.29e9 bytes) is refused, a 5 GB card (5.37e9) takes turns, and a 6 GB card (6.44e9) holds both, which is exactly what the page's bands predict. Nobody is misled today; the units still disagree.
source_verification.sibling_page_agreement: wiki/clients/windows.md:207-210 states the same mechanism in the same words, `the persona thinks and speaks one at a time, and you hear a short pause before a reply is spoken`, and names no video-memory figure of its own, so the two pages agree and neither contradicts the other.
source_verification.macos_half: Unmoved and correct. crates/hearth-probe/tests/plan_fixtures.rs:35-52 pins the m1-air-8gb fixture to tier 0 with `p.coexist` true and an explicit assertion that no warning contains `one at a time`, which is what the page's `an 8 GB M2 MacBook Air runs a persona and its voice at the same time` says. wiki/installing.md:50-52 says the same in the same register.
source_verification.persona_link: Correct. The page points at wiki/meeting-your-persona.md, the reader-facing walkthrough, and does not link wiki/first-run.md anywhere in the body. first-run.md remains in the frontmatter sources list, which is provenance rather than a reader-facing link.

found.location: §Check that your machine can run it
found.issue: The abstract promises the reader will find out "whether your machine can run it", and the Windows half answers only for a machine with a dedicated GPU: "On Windows, video memory decides the answer." crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:49-51 returns total system RAM as the pool when no GPU reports VRAM, and machine.rs:55-57 resolves the backend to `cpu`, so Hearth plans and installs on a Windows laptop with integrated graphics rather than declining. The page says nothing to that reader beyond the unquantified "a capable GPU", and no page in wiki/ states whether that configuration is supported.
found.fix: State what a Windows machine with no dedicated GPU gets, once someone has settled whether it is a supported configuration.
found.reason: Integrated graphics is the commonest Windows configuration there is. Such a reader either self-excludes on a hedge or downloads on the strength of the three bands, measures video memory they do not have, and cannot tell which band they are in.

detailed_review.score_reasoning: Baseline 10 - (F1 1 + F2 1 + F3 1 + F4 1) = 6, NEEDS_WORK. Four findings, each medium: the concept shape's fourth item thin to the point of absence (F1), a defining section that defined the wrong noun (F2), an unanswerable hardware question for the commonest Windows configuration (F3), and an artifact list that offered a phone reader the one file that does nothing alone (F4). F1 is graded 1 rather than the vocabulary's default 2 for missing-spine because severity follows reader consequence: the shape item was partly served by the interview paragraph, and what was missing was the concrete example and the figure rather than the whole section. After the run, 10 - (F3 1 + F5 0.5 + F6 0.5) = 8, PASS with minor nits open. F3 is the only substantial thing still open and it is open honestly: it needs a product fact nobody in this pipeline has established. F5 and F6 are half-point consistency items found during the single regrade. The cap at 9 for a non-empty remaining[] does not bind, because the arithmetic already lands at 8.
detailed_review.what_worked: F2 fixed the most expensive sentence on the page. This is the corpus's only entry point for a reader who does not have an installer, and its defining section defined a persona rather than the product, in the exact words wiki/features/personas.md:24 uses for a persona. A stranger now learns in one sentence that Hearth is an AI companion on their own machine that they talk to and that answers out loud. F1 gave the page the thing the concept shape asks for and the page had none of: something concrete to picture. §Live with your persona is 57 words and every clause traces to a page in the corpus, and it carries the page's first figure request, so the front door will eventually show the product rather than only describe it. F4 closed a small trap: the artifact list read as four equivalent choices, and a phone reader who took the `.apk` would have installed a window with no house behind it. Separately, the two claims this task exists to make both check out against source. The download statement matches wiki/releasing.md:37-42 and :208 artifact for artifact and to the day, the unsigned macOS caveat matches wiki/releasing.md:40 and lands the reader on wiki/installing.md:76-88 where the extra step actually lives, and the three Windows bands recompute exactly from crates/hearth-probe: refusal below 4466165856 bytes and both resident above 5432533497, which is the `roughly 4.5 GB` and `roughly 5.4 GB` the page states. The old 8 GB video-memory floor was wrong by nearly a factor of two, and wiki/clients/windows.md:207-210 states the same mechanism in the same words, so the sibling pages agree.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down: F3 is the real one. The abstract promises the reader will find out whether their machine can run Hearth, and for a Windows laptop with integrated graphics the page does not answer. Worse, the three bands invite that reader to measure video memory they do not have, while crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:49-51 quietly plans against their system RAM instead and machine.rs:55-57 puts the model on the processor. Nothing in wiki/ says whether that install is supported or usable, so the honest move was to block rather than to write a sentence. F5 and F6 are small and visible: the page tells the reader twice that Sulivan interviews them, and it calls a persona `it` one line above a section that calls them `they`, which argues against the product's own claim that you make someone rather than configure something. Beyond the findings, two things sit just under the bar. The band figures are decimal gigabytes while crates/hearth-probe/src/lib.rs:24-35 prints GiB under a `GB` label, on the stated grounds that GiB is what a reader comparing against a spec sheet expects, so the page's numbers run about eight percent above the ones the product will show a refused reader. And the version-and-date sentence in the download section goes stale silently at the next release, which the author already recorded as unresolved.
